x: Championships, Stu Paton teamed up with Seb Coe in the 1500m against France. 2nd fastest this year on paper Stu was expected to split the French runners.
Here we see John with Seb Coe representing the U.K in June's Russia match. In windy conditions and after setting the early pace John outkicked Olympic 1500m bronze medallist Kirov(4) for second.
Then we had Seb Coe warming up before the start and the huge crowd were well entertained. All told 124 athletes competed including 32 Senior/Junior athletes of International fame.
Following his UK Championships victory, John Gladwin was selected for international duty over the mile against the Soviet Union with Seb Coe as his partner in the two a side match.
But by far the most impressive run came from Mike Hayes who came in on the first leg in a close 8th place in a time which was to prove to be only 32 secs slower than Seb Coe's fastest leg of 16.16.

No doubt Seb Coe would have commanded a good fee. our man settled for £28. As it turned out the adventure had its brighter side.

Seb Coe, David Hemery etc. to both demonstrate and talk about the techniques involved in their events, but I came into the story because for the long jump they had Lyn Davies who was quite able to coach, but because of a long-standing injury didn't feel able to run and jump.

STAGE FOUR Dave handed to Andy who flew around the course passing team after team and chasing Steve Karens and Seb Coe. Andy ran the fifth fastest time of the day and Bels were in 7th - our highest position for many years.

Best performance came from John Gladwin when he towed Seb Coe round to break his own league record in the 800m. In the 'B' race John Booth came within a whisker of winning but nevertheless set a pb of 1.52.77.
